key_insight: A scalable xylene-assisted in-situ spray coating can deposit few-layer graphene onto copper with preserved copper crystallinity and a conductive, interconnected surface network.
engineering_relevance: This offers a low-cost, manufacturable route for graphene-enhanced copper surfaces in thermal management and heat-transfer applications.
method: Prepared a stable sprayable graphene dispersion using modified Hummers graphene in xylene/isopropanol with epoxy binder and suspension agents.
Spray-coated the dispersion onto copper substrates under controlled conditions.
Characterized the coating using XRD, Raman, FTIR, and SEM; estimated layer thickness and spacing from XRD analysis.
evidence_signal: XRD, Raman, FTIR, and SEM together confirmed few-layer graphene on copper, with interlayer spacing of 3.37 Å and an ID/IG drop from 2.1 to 0.85 after coating.
watch_item: The use of epoxy/binder and solvent-assisted spray conditions may affect long-term thermal performance, adhesion durability, and coating repeatability at larger scale.
paper_title: Structural characterization of graphene-coated copper substrate prepared by scalable In-Situ spray coating using xylene dispersion
